question: Related Questions Q. Zakah Calculations in the light of Sahih Ahadith 2301 views Q. I found some money (1 note of Bangladeshi 500 Taka, equivalent to US $7) at the Masjid premise (that leads to the entrance/exit of the Masjid and Madrasa), on January 18, 2008. Instantly I enquired to few people like Muazzin, Khadem of Masjid and some labours whether they lost any money. They said 'NO'. I thought it was lost from any worker (Madrasa-construction work was going on ) and hence enquired my best but found no one claiming the money. Then I requested the Muazzin to make a decleration after Isha Farz Salaah among the Musallis regarding the lost money. He did so. But no one came or claimed. Then I asked a local Ulama regarding the matter and he replied, I should wait for 2 months. If in the mean time no one came to claim the money, I should give the money to poor people. 1 (one) month has already passed. I'm confused about what to do with that note. Please provide me answers for the following queries on the basis of the written matter: 1). Should I really wait for another 1 month (total 2 months) to find the owner of the money? 2). What other types of decleration should I make to find the owner? Should I make some posters and paste them on the Masjid building? 3). If I can give the money to the poor right now, waiting no further, Should I give all the money to a single poor man/woman or I can give among 50 people at same or more & less proportionate. 4). If someone asks me for a loan of 500 Taka, Can I give him that note of 500 Taka since it's in my pocket for long 1 month without being used , finding no owner? Inshallah I can give the same amount if the real owner claims the money after I give the money to someone as loan. Please, read carefully and provide all the necessary and possible annwers with available options I have. ZazakAllah 1612 views Q. Query on old Zakaat Calculation 2028 views Q. answer: Prayers & Duties >> Zakat & Charity Question ID: 759 Country: LK Title: Conversion of Zakat Money to Regular Wealth and then use the same for Masjids, Madrasas and Dawah Work Question: Conversion of Zakat Money to Regular Wealth and then use the same for Masjids, Madrasas and Dawah Work We are living in a country of people with mixed fortunes, some are quite rich, and the majority of the people are in the middle class. We have a lower class which is dependent on Zakat for most of their needs and sometimes the middle class is also in need of Zakat for Housing, Wedding etc. I feel that if all the rich class use their Zakat Money in a proper way, then we can fill this gap and give a decent life to the lower class and solve the problem of the middle class. The following has become a practice with some of the people here, and I have heard that this is also in practice in countries like India and Pakistan: ?Zakat is given to a person who is poor and liable to receive Zakat, but the said person returns the money back, deducting a small amount, to a committee or individual. The returned money is considered as NON-ZAKAT and used to Build Masjids, Build and Run Madrasas and Used for Dawah Related Work. I kindly request Your Holiness to clarify the following: ? Is the above allowed? Can you please prove the same with Holy Quran and Hadees Shariff. ? If it is allowed in Shariat. Can you please give a stronger argument where this practice of conversion to be stopped, because with this practice we are depriving the rights of the genuine recipients of Zakat. Thanking you, Wassalaam Answer ID: 759 Posted on: Aug 31, 2020 Bismillah hir-Rahman nir-Rahim ! (Fatwa: 624/646/B) It is impermissible to use Zakah money for mosque expenses. It must be given to the poor and needy, only the poor have the right to receive it. The mosque and madrasa should be constructed and managed by donations (other than Zakah ) even on small scale. Allah (Subhana Wa Ta'ala) knows Best Darul Ifta, Darul Uloom Deoband, India
